questions.stem:
Consider the following assertion:

"In the Pleistocene period either the Yamuna once flowed into the Indus, or the Sutlej flowed into the Yamuna and one major tributary of either had shifted from the Ganga to the Indus or vice versa."
statements: The Nadi-Sukta of the Rigveda
The explorations of the Sutlej and the Yamuna by Robert Bruce Foote
The presence of the same species of dolphins in both the Indus and the Ganga river systems
questions.instruction: Which of the following is/are the basis of the above assertion?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 rejected: The Nadi-Sukta is a Vedic praise hymn of rivers - it records names, not geological shifts. No evidence of Pleistocene river capture. Statement 2 rejected: Foote's work was in South India (Pallavaram, Attirampakkam, Deccan Trap). He did not study or write about Sutlej-Yamuna in the context of Pleistocene river movements. Statement 3 confirmed: The taxonomic closeness of Platanista gangetica (Ganga) and Platanista minor (Indus) is the standard scientific evidence used to infer an ancient riverine connection between the two systems. Only Statement 3 is a valid basis → Answer: (d) 3
questions.source_note: 📚 NCERT Class 11 - India: Physical Environment (river systems chapter); Tamil Nadu SCERT Class 11 History; Wikipedia - South Asian river dolphin, Robert Bruce Foote, Nadistuti Sukta

questions.stem: What does an empty seat represent in early Buddhist iconography?
questions.explanation: In pre-Gandhara Buddhist art (before ~1st century CE), the Buddha was never shown in human form - his presence was indicated symbolically. Empty Seat / Empty Throne = the place where the Buddha sat in meditation → represents MEDITATION (Dhyana). Wheel (Dharmachakra) = First Sermon (Dharmachakrapravartana) at Sarnath → eliminates (b). Stupa = Mahaparinibbana (the passing away / death of the Buddha) → eliminates (c). Mahabhinishkramana = the Great Renunciation (Buddha leaving the palace). Symbolised by a horse with no rider or footprints - not an empty seat → eliminates (d). Answer: (a) The meditation of the Buddha
questions.source_note: 📚 NCERT Class 6 - Our Pasts I (Chapter on Buddhism); Tamil Nadu SCERT History; CUET Buddhist art matching questions (Collegedunia 2023); V&A Museum description of the Empty Throne sculpture

questions.subject: Ancient India
questions.stem: In which one among the following texts does the term kshetra-patni ('mistress of the field') originate?
questions.explanation: Kshetrapati ('lord/master of the field') is a tutelary deity appearing in both Rigveda and Atharvaveda. However, the FEMININE form - kshetra-patni ('mistress of the field') - appears specifically in the Atharvaveda Shaunakiya (AVŚ 2.12.1) and Vajasaneyi Samhita (VS 16.18). The Rigveda (a) uses kshetrasya pati (the lord form) - but the specific feminine 'kshetra-patni' is in Atharvaveda. Ashtadhyayi (c) is Panini's grammar text - it deals with linguistic rules, not agricultural mythology. Arthashastra (d) is Kautilya's political economy text - concerned with statecraft and taxation, not Vedic deities. Answer: (b) Atharvaveda
questions.source_note: 📚 Wikipedia - Kshetrapati (entry citing AVŚ 2.8.5 and 2.12.1, VS 16.18); Atharvaveda Shaunakiya; Academic sources on Vedic agricultural deities

questions.stem: Which one of the following Carnatic music ragas is similar to Raga Bilawal in Hindustani music?
questions.instruction: Which one of the following Carnatic music ragas is similar to Raga Bilawal in Hindustani music?
questions.explanation: Bilawal Thaat in Hindustani uses all natural (shuddha) swaras - S R G M P D N - equivalent to the Western major scale (Ionian mode). Its Carnatic equivalent is the 29th Melakarta raga: Dheera Shankarabharanam (commonly called Shankarabharanam). Both use the same set of natural notes. Nat Bhairavi (a): Corresponds to Natabhairavi - 20th Melakarta - equivalent to Asavari Thaat, not Bilawal. Kamavardhini (b): 51st Melakarta - equivalent to Purvi Thaat. Sharply different note pattern. Hanumatodi (c): 8th Melakarta - equivalent to Bhairavi Thaat (komal Re, Ga, Dha, Ni). Very different from Bilawal. Answer: (d) Dheera Shankarabharanam
questions.source_note: 📚 Standard Hindustani-Carnatic equivalence chart (Scribd/coursehero); Wikipedia - Bilawal, Sankarabharanam; Hindustani Carnatic Ragas Equivalent document

questions.stem: The artificially fixed rupee-sterling exchange rate prescribed by the Hilton-Young Commission (1926) was adopted by the British Government for which one of the following reasons?

options.text: Aiding the flow of remittances from India and maintaining India's creditworthiness
Encouraging export of cotton produce from India
Preventing depreciation of the Rupee in terms of gold

questions.explanation: The Hilton-Young Commission (1925-26) recommended fixing the rupee-sterling exchange rate at 1s 6d (one shilling and six pence) per rupee. The Hilton-Young Commission's primary stated rationale for fixing the exchange rate: to prevent depreciation of the Rupee in terms of gold and ensure currency stability - anchoring the rupee to gold/sterling at 1s 6d. Option (a) - Remittances + creditworthiness: While Home Charges benefited from the stable rate, this was not the Commission's primary stated rationale. Not correct ✗ Option (b) - Indian importers: Not the reason ✗ Option (c) - Cotton exports: Not the reason ✗ Option (d) - Preventing rupee depreciation in terms of gold: The Commission recommended fixing the rate to provide monetary stability and prevent the rupee from depreciating against gold. This is the correct official rationale ✓ Answer: (d) Aiding the flow of remittances from India and maintaining India's creditworthiness
questions.source_note: 📚 The Book Notes - Monetary Policy in British India (UGC NET History Notes); historydiscussion.net - Indian Currency System; Dr. B.R. Ambedkar - The Problem of the Rupee (cited by Hilton-Young Commission)

questions.subject: Modern History
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the Eka Movement and Bardoli Satyagraha is correct?
questions.instruction: Which one of the following statements about the Eka Movement and Bardoli Satyagraha is correct?

options.text: The Eka Movement was throughout supported and organized by the Congress while Bardoli Satyagraha was initially independent of Congress influence and was only in the last stages supported by the Congress.
The Eka Movement was provided leadership by the taluqdars of Awadh, whereas the Bardoli Satyagraha was a movement of the landless labourers.
The Bardoli Satyagraha was a campaign against the enhancement of land revenue, while the Eka Movement was a protest against excessive extraction of rents.
The Eka Movement was located in the Varanasi and Mirzapur districts of the present-day U.P., while the Bardoli Satyagraha took place in Saurashtra.

questions.explanation: Eka Movement (1921): Awadh (Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur districts, UP). Protest against EXORBITANT RENTS charged by taluqdars/zamindars (often 50%+ above recorded rent). Initially given push by Congress and Khilafat leaders; later led by low-caste Madari Pasi - then lost Congress connection. Bardoli Satyagraha (1928): Bardoli taluka, Surat district, Gujarat (Bombay Presidency, part of Saurashtra region). Led by Vallabhbhai Patel. Campaign against a 22-30% enhancement of LAND REVENUE (government tax), not rents. Congress-organised throughout. Option (a): Wrong - Eka Movement did NOT have Congress support throughout; Bardoli was NOT independent of Congress initially - it was Congress-organised from the start. Option (b): Wrong - Eka movement leaders were NOT taluqdars (taluqdars were the oppressors); Bardoli was not a landless labourers' movement. Option (c): ✅ CORRECT - Bardoli = against land revenue enhancement; Eka = against excessive rent extraction. This is accurate. Option (d): Wrong - Eka Movement was in Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur (not Varanasi/Mirzapur). Bardoli is in Surat district, Gujarat - technically part of present Saurashtra broadly but more precisely Surat/South Gujarat. Answer: (c)
questions.source_note: 📚 Wikipedia - Eka Movement, Bardoli Satyagraha; Drishti IAS - Peasant Movements; Rau's IAS Modern History; NCERT Class 12 - India's Struggle for Independence (Bipan Chandra)
